subject: POC trial planning follow-up / workload intake - Acme Health
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Katie Rogers <katie@acmehealth.com>, John Lee <john.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: POC trial planning & workload intake (next steps)

Hi Katie / John —

Thanks again for a great discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the POC success criteria and workload intake we discussed:  

1) Success criteria (what Acme Health needs to validate):
   - <Strong inference latency> 95th percentile <= 300ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and <= 600ms for long prompts (~1k tokens) under baseline load.
   - <Cost/throughput target> average token cost target of <= $0.0009 per token when running at expected QPS for the evaluation set.
   - <Quality> generation F1 / human-eval pass rate >= your internal threshold (we'll instrument a small eval set).

2) Evaluation plan / timelines:
   - Week 0 (this week): exchange workload profile (RPS, typical prompt lengths, concurrency patterns).
   - Week 1: Redwood spins up a dedicated trial environment, deploys recommended model variant + quantization.
   - Week 2: Run test harness with your workload for 72 hours, capture latency/cost/quality telemetry.
   - Week 3: Analyze results, iterate on batching/quantization, and share final report.

3) Workload & traffic profile we need from Acme (examples):
   - Baseline RPS (average) and peak RPS / burst pattern (e.g., 10m bursts to 200 RPS once per day)
   - Typical and max token lengths for requests (prompt + expected completion)
   - Concurrent open connections (expected concurrency), KV cache hit rates if applicable
   - Any cold-start patterns (e.g., daily morning ramp at 8:00 AM local)

4) Ownership & internal contacts:
   - Acme lead: Katie Rogers (we'll work with John for infra specifics)
   - Redwood: Dylan (technical lead / trial ops), Ben (solutions & SRE sizing), Marissa (CS / success criteria).

5) Attachments / links: please share a CSV or simple JSON with sample RPS timeline and token length distribution. We can also accept a small sample log (redacted).

I'll put Ben and Marissa on copy to help with sizing and success criteria. If this looks right, can you please: (a) share the workload_profile.csv by EOD Thursday, and (b) confirm the two-week window is acceptable?

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

--
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: poc-evaluation-plan.pdf (summary of proposed plan)

From: Katie Rogers <katie@acmehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: John Lee <john.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC trial planning & workload intake (next steps)

Thanks Dylan — this is perfect and aligns with what we discussed. Quick answers and notes below:  

- We're good with the two-week trial window (week of 6/7 for baseline run).
- We'll provide the workload profile as a CSV by EOD Thursday (6/3).

Workload summary (high-level):
- Baseline average RPS: 35 RPS (US peak hours)
- Typical daily peak: 180 RPS for ~10-15 minute bursts (happens 2–3x/day)
- Concurrent open requests: ~40 during peak; long tail of short requests during off-peak
- Token lengths: median prompt 75 tokens; median completion 40 tokens; 95th percentile total tokens ~820
- KV cache: low reuse for us (most prompts unique), so KV cache hit rate ~5%
- Cold-start pattern: daily ramp 7:30–9:30 AM PST, steady mid-day, short evening spikes.

I'll attach the CSV (sample timeline + token distribution) in my next email — sharing with John to confirm infra details.

Best,
Katie
Director of Product, Acme Health
Katie.Rogers@acmehealth.com

Attachment: (will attach acme_workload_profile.csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Katie Rogers <katie@acmehealth.com>, John Lee <john.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC trial planning & workload intake (next steps)

Thanks — good data from Katie. A few technical notes on sizing / configs we'll try for the Week 1 run:  

- Target instance mix: 2 x a2-standard-equivalent GPUs for warm baseline, autoscale to handle bursts (short 10–15 minute spikes).
- Batching policy: small-opportunistic batching (50–200ms max hold) for short requests, dynamic window for long prompt runs.
- Quantization: start with 4-bit quantized variant (if model supports) to reduce token cost; we can rollback if quality regresses.
- Latency SLOs: will instrument p95 and p99; p99 expectations may be > p95 during bursts but we'll capture and recommend mitigations (prefetching, route to higher-tier instances).

Dylan: I'll own the autoscaling config and instance selection. Marissa: can you own the trial success checklist and coordinate the evaluation set?

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Katie Rogers <katie@acmehealth.com>, John Lee <john.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC trial planning & workload intake (next steps)

I'll take ownership of the success checklist. Proposed eval items to instrument during the run:  

- Automated latency traces per route (p50/p95/p99)
- Token cost per request and aggregated cost-per-hour
- Quality: run a 200-sample eval set (we'll need 200 labeled prompts from Acme or permission to sample)
- Error rates and graceful degradation checks (fallback routing working)
- Stability: no more than 1 unrecoverable error per 100k requests

Katie — can you confirm whether you can provide the 200-sample labeled eval set or if Redwood should sample from live traffic (anonymized)?

Thanks — I'll draft the checklist and send a shared doc.

--
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Katie Rogers <katie@acmehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-03T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC trial planning & workload intake (next steps)

Hi all — attaching the CSV with our workload profile and a short note on the labeled eval set. Summary here:  

- Attached CSV: 24h timeline (one-minute granularity) with RPS and median token lengths.
- Eval set: we can provide a 200-sample labeled set (redacted PHI removed) by Monday 6/07; for the Week 1 run, please start with our supplied sample traffic and pause any live-sampling until we confirm redaction.

We'll also add John to provide temporary firewall rules for Redwood's trial IPs; John, can you confirm network access is OK for the dedicated trial region?

Thanks — sending CSV now.

Best,
Katie

Attachment: acme_workload_profile.csv

From: John Lee <john.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Katie Rogers <katie@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-03T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC trial planning & workload intake (next steps)

All good from infra — we've provisioned a temporary allowlist for Redwood trial IP range and opened ports for TLS traffic. Dylan / Ben: I'll share the allowlist details over secure Slack/Confluence shortly.

One note: during the 10–15 minute bursts, our internal monitoring shows upstream retries increase (we think due to max concurrency limits on our side). If we see elevated p99s during your test run, we may need to coordinate retry/backoff tuning together.

John Lee
Head of Platform, Acme Health
john.lee@acmehealth.com
